failure_patterns.pattern: strength_mismatch: Selected stronger claims from intuition—a witness-producing algorithm, a familiar variation threshold, or an invariant-only conclusion—without support from the stated result.

rejected_edits.content: For an equivalence, check both directions. For case splits or counting conditions, compare each branch literally, including equality versus strict inequality, allowed index classes, and exactly one versus at most one. Keep local or per-degree existence distinct from a globally coherent or multiplicative family.

Before ranking options, verify each distinguishing clause independently; choose the strongest claim actually supported, not the strongest-sounding one. An existential example does not establish a universal bound; a range of possible parameter values does not establish that every value is realized; existence of a solution does not establish least energy; and a named decomposition or kernel dimension does not by itself establish additional non-symmetry fields. Treat words such as “every,” “all,” and “conversely” as added quantifiers requiring evidence. Preserve whether the question asks for an existence claim or a universal one, and compare options only after checking their exact conclusions.

rejected_edits.content: For growth exponents defined by a liminf, translate the claim into counting inequalities before comparing options. If liminf as N tends to infinity of log A(N) / log N is at least alpha, then for every epsilon > 0, eventually A(N) >= N^(alpha - epsilon); this does not necessarily imply A(N) >= c N^alpha for a fixed c > 0. Check endpoint exponents and constant-factor claims separately.
